definition: An analysis that computes the average value of a variable over each year.
comment: Annual means summarize the overall level of a resource and allow years to be compared, for example to identify windier or sunnier years.

definition: An analysis that groups observations or locations into classes of similar characteristics.
comment: Clustering is used to define zones with similar resource behaviour, such as solar radiation zones, or to group measurement stations.

definition: An analysis that measures the strength of association between two or more variables.
comment: Correlation is used, for example, to relate rainfall to hydropower generation or to select the input variables of a model.

definition: An analysis that checks and corrects data for errors, inconsistencies or missing values before use.
comment: Quality control ensures that the measurements used to characterize a resource are reliable, for example by detecting gaps or implausible values.

definition: An analysis that summarizes data with statistics such as mean, variance, minimum and maximum.
comment: Descriptive statistics give a first quantitative picture of a dataset, describing its central value, spread and shape without drawing inferences.

definition: An analysis of existing documents such as reports, policies, statistics or literature.
comment: Documentary analysis is used to review the state of a sector, its policies or its projects from published sources rather than new measurements.

definition: An analysis of the probability of rare, extreme values of a variable, such as maximum wind speeds.
comment: Extreme value distributions such as Gumbel are used to estimate design values, for example the wind speed expected once in fifty years.

definition: An analysis that describes the percentage of time a river flow, or the power it can produce, is equalled or exceeded.
comment: Flow and power duration curves are the basis for estimating the dependable flow and sizing run-of-river and small hydropower plants.

definition: An analysis that describes how often the values of a variable occur, usually by fitting a probability distribution.
comment: For wind energy this typically means describing wind speeds with a Weibull or similar distribution, from which the energy content of the wind can be derived.

definition: An analysis that uses a statistical test to decide whether data support a stated hypothesis.
comment: Statistical tests check, for example, whether two periods of wind data come from the same distribution.

definition: An analysis of information collected through interviews with experts or stakeholders.
comment: Interview analysis captures detailed qualitative knowledge from people involved in a sector, such as developers, officials or communities.

definition: An analysis that computes the average value of a variable for each month.
comment: Monthly means reveal how a resource varies through the year and are commonly used to size systems and plan energy production.

definition: An analysis that reduces many correlated variables to a few uncorrelated components.
comment: Principal component analysis reveals the main patterns of joint variation in a dataset, for example between wind and solar resources.

definition: An analysis that estimates the relationship between a dependent variable and one or more explanatory variables.
comment: Regression quantifies how a variable responds to others, for example how hydropower reliability depends on climatic or operational factors.

definition: An analysis that computes the average value of a variable for each season.
comment: Seasonal means show how a resource differs between wet and dry, or summer and winter, periods, which matters for matching supply and demand.

definition: An analysis of how the variation of a result depends on variations of its inputs or parameters.
comment: Sensitivity analysis identifies the inputs that most influence an outcome, such as the model parameters that control simulated river flow or the cost factors that drive energy prices.

definition: An analysis that studies data using their geographic location, typically with a geographic information system.
comment: Spatial analysis maps resources, screens and ranks candidate sites, and combines criteria such as slope, distance and resource level into suitability maps.

definition: An analysis of answers collected through questionnaires.
comment: Survey analysis summarizes the views of a sample of respondents, for example the barriers investors perceive to renewable energy projects.

definition: An analysis that identifies and organizes recurring themes in qualitative information.
comment: Thematic analysis groups evidence such as reported barriers or motivations into categories that explain a situation.

definition: An analysis that detects and quantifies long-term increases or decreases in a variable.
comment: Trend tests such as Mann-Kendall reveal whether a resource has changed over decades, which matters for long-term energy planning.

definition: An analysis of the short-term fluctuation of wind speed relative to its mean.
comment: Turbulence intensity affects turbine loads, fatigue and energy output, and is used to choose suitable turbine classes for a site.

definition: An analysis that quantifies the uncertainty of a result arising from uncertain inputs, parameters or data.
comment: Uncertainty analysis expresses results with ranges or probabilities, for example through Monte Carlo simulation or prediction intervals.

definition: An analysis of how a variable, typically wind speed, changes with height above ground.
comment: Wind speed increases with height, so vertical profile laws such as the power law or log law are used to estimate wind at turbine hub height from lower measurements.

definition: An analysis of the frequency of wind directions at a location, usually represented by a wind rose.
comment: Knowing the prevailing wind directions helps orient and space wind turbines and assess how terrain and obstacles affect the wind.
